title: HFrEF follow-up: ivabradine start
description: Chronic HFrEF on optimized GDMT with persistent resting tachycardia. Clinician starts ivabradine. Every simulated policy criterion is stated in the transcript.
synthetic_notice: Entirely fictional. Not derived from any real patient or encounter.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Varga. Last time I saw you was right after your hospital stay in March. How have things been since then?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Better than March, for sure. But I still get winded going up the stairs at home. I have to stop halfway up, every time.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Any trouble breathing when you lie flat? Waking up at night short of breath?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: No, I sleep on one pillow. That part is fine.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: How about swelling in your ankles?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: A little by the end of the day. It's gone by the morning.

segments.speaker: staff
segments.text: Vitals are in. Blood pressure 112 over 70, heart rate 78 sitting, weight 196 pounds, oxygen 97 percent on room air.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Thank you. Let's go through your medications. Metoprolol succinate 200 milligrams once a day?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yes, every morning.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Entresto 49/51, twice a day?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Twice a day, yes.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Spironolactone 25 milligrams daily and Farxiga 10 milligrams daily?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Both of those. And the furosemide 40 in the morning.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Any dizziness when you stand up?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Not really. Maybe once last week when I got up too fast.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Your echo from June 12th showed an ejection fraction of 30 percent, about where it was in the hospital. The ECG we did today shows normal sinus rhythm.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: So it hasn't gotten better.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Not yet. Your chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction is stable, but your heart rate is still in the upper 70s, and you're already on the maximum dose of metoprolol, so I don't want to push it any further.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Functionally I'd put you at NYHA class III today. You're comfortable at rest, but less than ordinary activity, like one flight of stairs, brings on symptoms.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Have you ever been told you have atrial fibrillation or an irregular heartbeat?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: No, nobody has ever said that to me.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Good. There's a medication called ivabradine that slows the heart rate for people in normal rhythm. It can lower the chance of ending up back in the hospital.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Another pill twice a day?

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Twice a day. I'm going to start you on ivabradine 5 milligrams twice daily, and we'll recheck your heart rate in two weeks.

segments.speaker: clinician
segments.text: Your insurance will likely need paperwork for this one, so our team will send that in. Keep taking everything else the same.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Okay. Same as before, plus the new one once it's approved.
